title: U.S. House · Colorado's 8th District
area: North Denver suburbs and Weld County, including Thornton, Greeley and Brighton.

context.text: Ballotpedia identified this as a battleground race for the November 3, 2026 general election. Incumbent Gabe Evans (R) defeated Yadira Caraveo (D) 49.0%-48.2% in 2024, in a district that President Trump won by less than 2 points in 2024. Manny Rutinel won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary over State Rep. Shannon Bird and Evan Munsing (who unofficially withdrew); Rutinel was appointed to the Colorado House of Representatives in 2023 and did not seek re-election there in 2026. As of June 30, 2026, Evans had raised $5.39 million and Rutinel had raised $4.34 million.

summary.text: Gabe Evans is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 8th District, elected in 2024 after defeating incumbent Yadira Caraveo. He is an Army veteran and former police lieutenant who previously served two years in the Colorado House of Representatives.

background.text: Born in Aurora, Colorado; served in the U.S. Army from 2007 to 2019; earned a bachelor's degree from Patrick Henry College in 2009.
Career experience includes owning and operating a family farm, working as a police lieutenant, and serving as a concealed-carry firearms instructor.
Served in the Colorado House of Representatives (District 48) from 2023 to 2025 before his election to Congress in 2024.

priorities.text: Campaign website lists four platform pillars: lowering the cost of living by reducing deficit spending and regulation, focusing the military on "warfighting," expanding educational choice for families, and "defending American values."
priorities.quote: Lower the cost of living by reining in deficit spending and the tax-and-regulate policies that are crushing our economy.

positions.summary: Campaign website says educational freedom means families should be able to choose the education that works best for them.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security (Counterterrorism and Intelligence; Emergency Management and Technology subcommittees) and the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Energy; Environment subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Manny Rutinel
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary over State Rep. Shannon Bird and Evan Munsing (who unofficially withdrew).
candidates.currentRole: Member, Colorado House of Representatives, District 32 (2023-2026)

summary.text: Manny Rutinel is a Colorado state representative and attorney running for Colorado's 8th District. He was appointed to the state House in 2023 and did not run for re-election there in 2026, instead running for Congress.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Florida in 2016, a master's degree from Johns Hopkins University in 2018, and a J.D. from Yale Law School in 2022.
Professional experience includes working as an economist at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and as chief executive officer of Climate Refarm.

An Adams County Democratic vacancy committee appointed him to the Colorado House of Representatives, District 32, on October 9, 2023, to replace Dafna Michaelson Jenet; he left that office on September 4, 2026 to focus on the congressional race.

priorities.text: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response, said he is running in part to oppose planned cuts to the Social Security Administration's workforce and field offices.
priorities.quote: Trump, Gabe Evans, and their billionaire donors plan to lay off half the Social Security workforce and shutter field offices, causing delay, disruption, and denial of earned benefits. It's a backdoor cut that inflicts pain on seniors and people with disabilities, and I'm running to stop it.

positions.summary: Says planned cuts to the Social Security Administration's staffing and field offices would delay and deny benefits to seniors and people with disabilities, and says he is running to stop them.
positions.quote: Trump, Gabe Evans, and their billionaire donors plan to lay off half the Social Security workforce and shutter field offices, causing delay, disruption, and denial of earned benefits.

record.text: Served as a member of the Colorado House of Representatives, District 32, from October 2023 until leaving office on September 4, 2026.

summary.text: David Wood is the Libertarian Party candidate for Colorado's 8th District.
